body.translated_text: Om, homage to the supreme guru <s>Gorakṣanātha</s>.

children.translated_text: Om, I will recite the Gorakṣa-śataka.
For liberation from the bonds of existence.
The key to the door of discernment.
This is the stairway to liberation.
This is the deception of time.
When the mind is turned away from delusion.
Of the branch served by the twice-born.
The fruit of the tree of Vedic knowledge.
There are species of living beings.
Are known by the great lord.
A hundred and sixteen are made.
Placing the heel at the base of the genitals, one should firmly establish.

children.text: meḍhre pādam athaikam eva niyataṃ kṛtvā samaṃ vigraham
children.translated_text: Then placing one foot on the genitals, keeping the body straight.
Like a pillar, with controlled senses, gazing steadily at the space between the eyebrows.
This is called <s>Siddhāsana</s>, the opener of the gate of liberation.

children.text: vāmorūpari dakṣiṇaṃ hi caraṇaṃ saṃsthāpya vāmaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Placing the right foot over the left thigh and the left foot likewise.

children.text: dakṣorūpari paścimena vidhinā dhṛtvā karābhyāṃ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Holding firmly with the hands, in the manner of the ancients.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhau hṛdaye nidhāya cibukaṃ nāsāgram ālokayed
children.translated_text: Placing the thumbs on the heart, gaze at the tip of the nose.
This is called <s>Padmāsana</s>, the destroyer of diseases for the self-controlled.
The base is the first chakra.
The place of the yoni is between the two.
In the place called <s>Ādhāra</s> at the anus.
There is a lotus with four petals.
In its center is said to be the yoni.
In the center of the yoni is the great <s>Liṅga</s>.
At the head, like a jewel, divided.
He who knows this is a knower of yoga.
Flashing like a streak of lightning.
It is said to be below the genitals.
Where the bulb is through the <s>Suṣumṇā</s>.
Above the genitals, below the navel.
The bulb-yoni is like a bird's egg.
Should always be known by yogis.
<s>Iḍā</s> is situated on the left side.
Thus, at the doors are established.
The five starting with <s>Nāga</s> are well-known.
Exist in the form of life.
The life under the control of <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>.
Through the left and right paths.
Due to restlessness, it is not seen.
Struck on the ground with a stick.
Like a falcon bound by a cord.
Even gone, it is drawn back.
Similarly, life is bound by qualities.
These two are situated above and below.
He who knows this is a knower of yoga.
Above the bulb is the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> power.
Always at the opening of the <s>Brahma-dvāra</s>.
It remains covering with its mouth.
Awakened by the union with fire.
Struck by the mind and wind.
That yogi is a vessel of perfection.

children.text: vakṣo-nyasta-hanur nipīḍya suciraṃ yoniṃ ca vāmāṅghriṇā
children.translated_text: Pressing the chin on the chest and the yoni with the left heel for a long time.

children.text: hastābhyām avadhāritaṃ prasaritaṃ pādaṃ tathā dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Holding the extended foot with the hands, also the right.

children.text: āpūrya śvasanena kukṣi-yugalaṃ baddhvā śanai recayed
children.translated_text: Filling the pair of bellies with breath, then slowly exhaling.

children.text: eṣā pātaka-nāśinī sumahatī mudrā nṝṇāṃ procyate
children.translated_text: This is called the great sin-destroying mudrā for people.
The tongue in the cavity of the skull.
The gaze fixed between the eyebrows.
Above the genitals, below the navel.
The lion to the elephant of death.
When the bond of <s>Jālandhara</s> is made.
Characterized by the contraction of the throat.
The nectar does not fall into the fire.
Nor does the wind become agitated.
When the wind moves, all moves.
The swan is thirty-six fingers long.
Through the left and right paths.
With gaze on the tip of the nose, alone.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the wind residing in the body.
Then the yogi becomes like the sky.
Should fill the <s>Prāṇa</s> with the moon.
Meditating at the navel, the yogi.
In the superior, thrice the units.
In the lower, there is intense heat.
In the superior, the yogi rises.
Abandoning pungent, sour, and salty foods.
Do not excessively restrain the wind.
The head is led by force.
The destroyer of the fuel of sin.
The great bridge over the ocean of sin.
One woman is enjoyed by two.
The third who is with them.
In the navel region is one.
The immortal soul is always situated.
And the moon at the root of the palate.
The method is to be known there.
Above the navel, below the palate.
The upward sun, the downward moon.
Is obtained from the guru's mouth.
Where the bull is tied threefold.
And the <s>Anāhata</s> that is the wheel.
Known in the heart of the yogi.
When the great lotus is reached by <s>Prāṇa</s>.
The wheel is known by the knowers of the wheel.
having held the water of the lunar digit (<s>soma-kalā</s>),
within a month it does not diminish,
having deceived the mouth of the sun.
Pressing with the tip of the tongue
the great cavity of the royal tooth,
meditating on the goddess made of nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) —
within six months one becomes a poet (<s>kavi</s>).
For the yogin whose body is filled with nectar,
the arising of qualities such as <s>aṇimā</s> [atomic minuteness] and others [occurs].
Just as fire [does not leave] its fuel,
and a lamp [does not leave] its oil-wick,
so the embodied one whose [body] is filled with the lunar digit
In the heart, the <s>dhāraṇā</s> of the five elements
through the steadiness of the mind,
The earth [element], beautiful as the region of yellow orpiment, yellow, associated with the syllable 'la',

children.text: saṃyuktā kamalāsanena hi catuṣkoṇā hṛdi sthāyinī
children.translated_text: conjoined with the lotus-seated [<s>Brahmā</s>], four-cornered, abiding in the heart —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.

children.text: eṣā stambhakarī sadā kṣitijayaṃ kuryād bhuvo dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the earth <s>dhāraṇā</s>, which causes immobility and always brings mastery over the earth.
Resembling a half-moon, white as <s>kunda</s> flowers, the water element stationed in the throat,
endowed with the seed-syllable 'va' of nectar, always conjoined with <s>Viṣṇu</s> —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.
This is the water <s>dhāraṇā</s>, which should be the remedy for the unbearable poison of <s>Kāla</s> [Death].
The element stationed at the palate, resembling an <s>indragopa</s> [firefly], brilliant and triangular,
consisting of fire and the syllable 'ra', beautiful as coral, conjoined with <s>Rudra</s> —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.

children.text: eṣā vahni-jayaṃ sadā vidadhate vaiśvānarī dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the <s>vaiśvānara</s> [fire] <s>dhāraṇā</s>, which always brings mastery over fire.

children.text: yad bhinnāñjana-puñja-sānnibham idaṃ tattvaṃ bhruvor antare
children.translated_text: That element between the eyebrows, resembling a mass of crushed collyrium,
circular, consisting of air, associated with the syllable 'ya', where <s>Īśvara</s> is the deity —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.

children.text: eṣā khe gamanaṃ karoti yamināṃ syād vāyavī dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the air <s>dhāraṇā</s> of the disciplined, which causes movement through the sky.
The space [element], resembling perfectly pure water, stationed in the <s>brahmarandhra</s> [crown aperture],
therein, always conjoined with <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the peaceful syllable 'ha' —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.
This is the space <s>dhāraṇā</s>, declared to be skilled in breaking open the door of liberation.
are the five <s>dhāraṇās</s> of the elements.
By action, by mind, and by speech,
the five <s>dhāraṇās</s> are difficult to attain.
The yogin who practices them constantly
When the mind is established in the ultimate reality (<s>tattva</s>),
<s>Saguṇa</s> is through the distinction of colors [forms];
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one is freed from sin.
beautifully adorned like a fine ruby —
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one is freed from transgression.
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one agitates the world.
Like lightning's radiance in the heart-lotus,
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one becomes filled with <s>Brahman</s>.
Constantly, in the middle of the bell [throat center],
the pure one, from which nectar arises —
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one becomes filled with <s>Brahman</s>.
The deity situated between the eyebrows,
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one becomes filled with bliss (<s>ānanda</s>).
in the sky, facing all directions —
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one is freed from suffering.
The anus, the genitals, the navel,
between the eyebrows — the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>),
pure, of the nature of space,
meditating on the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) as all-pervading,
[those] endowed with the reality of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>)
produce the arising of the eight powers (<s>guṇa</s>).
differently according to the color [placed near it].
When freed from the distinctions of power (<s>śakti</s>),
knowers of reality (<s>tattva</s>) know the reality.
The five sense-objects beginning with sound,
as long as they are perceived in the ears and other [senses],
only that long is meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) remembered;
then the oneness of equal essence (<s>samarasa</s>)
Neither smell, nor taste, nor form,
the yogin knows neither self nor other,
As milk [is hidden] in milk, ghee in ghee,
the knower of yoga, in the supreme state.
Fire in the forest of the fear of worldly existence,
the knower of yoga, in the supreme state.
